title: Application of Single-Cell Damage in Murine Intestinal Organoid Models
author: Seidler, Donath, et al.

steps.title: Isolate murine colonic crypts
steps.instruction: Precool a centrifuge to 4 °C and pre‑incubate a 24‑well plate at 37 °C. Sacrifice a 6–14 week C57BL/6J mouse by CO₂ overdose followed by cervical dislocation (confirm spinal cord disconnection). Disinfect abdomen with 70 % ethanol, open peritoneum, and excise the distal colon (≈2–3 cm distal to the caecum to ≈1 cm proximal to the anus) while minimizing attached fat. Flush the colon with 10 mL cold 1× PBS using a 10 mL syringe, place it on ice, and remove residual fat. Cut the colon lengthwise, rinse the apical side with cold PBS if needed, then cut into ~0.5 cm² pieces and transfer into 15 mL cold 2 mM EDTA in 1× PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free) (tube A). Seal tube A, shake horizontally on ice for 30 min. Let tissue settle and discard supernatant. Wash tissue twice with 5 mL 2 mM EDTA in PBS, swiveling gently, then let settle. Replace supernatant with 5 mL Dissection buffer, seal, wrap to protect from body heat, and shake vigorously for 7 min. Transfer the cloudy supernatant through a 70 µm cell strainer into a new 15 mL tube (tube B). Wash tube A twice with Dissection buffer and add those washes through the same strainer to tube B. Centrifuge tube B for 10 min at 500 × g, 4 °C. Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 5 mL cold 1× PBS. Centrifuge 5 min at 750 × g, 4 °C and keep on ice.

steps.title: Embed crypts in extracellular matrix
steps.instruction: Discard the PBS supernatant and resuspend the crypt pellet in 0.5–1 mL of a 40 % organoid media / 60 % Cultrex Reduced Growth Factor Basement Membrane Extract (BME, Type R1) mixture, avoiding air bubbles (≈500 µL total, aiming for ~10–20 crypts per 10 µL). Plate three 30 µL droplets of this suspension per well of the pre‑warmed 24‑well plate. Solidify the droplets for 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Culture organoids and change media
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL pre‑warmed conditioned organoid media supplemented with 10 µM Y‑27632 to each well and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Change media every two days; increase Y‑27632 to 20 µM only during the first two days after isolation.

steps.title: Plate HEK293T cells for transfection
steps.instruction: Ensure HEK293T cells in T175 flasks are 90–100 % confluent. Remove media, wash with 5 mL pre‑warmed 1× PBS per flask, and discard. Add 5 mL pre‑warmed Trypsin‑0.25 % EDTA, incubate 3 min at 37 °C to detach cells. Rinse each flask with 10 mL cell‑culture media, collect the cell suspension in a tube, and centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g. Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL media, make a 1:10 dilution, and count cells. Plate 6 × 10⁶ cells in 10 mL media into each of eight 100 mm dishes and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Check transfection efficiency
steps.instruction: If the transgene encodes a fluorescent protein, examine cells 24 h post‑transfection under a fluorescence microscope for signal. Ensure any signaling‑pathway‑sensitive transgene is expressed in HEK293T cells.

steps.title: First virus harvest (48 h)
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant from the eight 100 mm dishes into 50 mL tubes. Replace the spent media with 10 mL pre‑warmed media per dish supplemented with 20 mM HEPES and 1 mM sodium butyrate, then incubate another 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Centrifuge the harvested media 10 min at 2000 × g, preferably at 4 °C. Filter the clarified supernatant through a 0.45 µm sterile filter and store at 4 °C for 16–26 h. Prepare the ultracentrifuge rotor at 4 °C for the next harvest.

steps.title: Second virus harvest and concentrate (72 h)
steps.instruction: Harvest the supernatant from the eight dishes into 50 mL tubes, centrifuge 10 min at 2000 × g, 4 °C, and filter through a 0.45 µm sterile filter (total volume ≈160 mL). Concentrate virus by ultracentrifugation: transfer ~32 mL of filtered supernatant into each ultracentrifuge (UC) tube; fill a 5 mL serological pipette up to 7 mL with sucrose cushion solution, place the tip at the bottom of the UC tube and slowly pipette 2 mL of cushion underneath the media (repeat for each tube). Adjust each UC tube to the same weight by adding 1× PBS if needed. Place tubes in precooled rotor inserts and centrifuge at 100 000 × g for 2 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend and store viral aliquots
steps.instruction: Remove UC tubes, discard supernatant by tilting, and place tubes upside down on lint‑free tissue to dry for 5 min. Wipe inner tube walls with a lint‑free tissue, then resuspend each pellet in a total of 1 mL organoid media (or PBS if the virus will be used for other cell types). Mix thoroughly. Aliquot and store virus at –80 °C.

steps.title: Seed organoids for laser ablation
steps.instruction: Culture organoids in a 35 mm glass‑bottom dish (e.g., ibidi). When seeding, spread the organoid‑containing Cultrex as flat as possible so organoids lie close to the dish bottom.

steps.title: Set up femtosecond laser system
steps.instruction: Turn on the femtosecond laser, pre‑heat and gas the incubation chamber to 37 °C and 5 % CO₂ if available. Select the excitation wavelength and emission filter appropriate for the fluorophore (e.g., 730 nm excitation for green fluorophores with a 510–560 nm band‑pass filter). For autofluorescence imaging of NADH/FAD, use a blue filter (460 ± 20 nm).

steps.title: Adjust laser parameters
steps.instruction: Set laser power to 1–1.25 nJ for imaging. For single‑cell ablation at the crypt base, use 1.25–3.2 nJ; for ablation in differentiated epithelium, increase up to 4.4 nJ. Begin at the lower limit and increase in 0.125 nJ steps as needed. Ensure the photomultiplier tube (PMT) is never exposed to strong ambient light.

steps.title: Perform single‑cell ablation
steps.instruction: Locate the target cell (e.g., crypt neck) using the chosen fluorophore or autofluorescence. Apply the laser at the selected power (e.g., 2.5 nJ) and a scan speed of 10 µm/s to create a localized wound. Verify ablation by the increase in autofluorescence signal at the site.

steps.title: Acquire time‑lapse images
steps.instruction: Capture confocal images of the organoid before and after ablation, recording z‑stacks over the desired time course while maintaining the incubation conditions (37 °C, 5 % CO₂).

steps.title: Analyze images with Cellpose workflow
steps.instruction: Install Cellpose 2.0 for 2D segmentation. Split acquired z‑stacks into individual planes (or use the 3D stack). Run Cellpose on each plane to generate label images. Convert label images to ROIs using the ImageJ plugin ‘LabelsToROIs’. Analyze ROIs in ImageJ (or with custom macros) to extract cell morphology parameters (area, perimeter, aspect ratio, etc.). Map each measurement to its distance from the ablation site (µm) and perform statistical analysis with GraphPad Prism or OriginPro.

description: This protocol demonstrates how to generate highly localized wounding in murine colon organoids via a femtosecond laser system and subsequent live visualization of dynamic processes during intestinal regeneration. However, we also applied the ablation process on murine ileal organoids (Figure S1) and together with the transduction protocol, imaging procedure and analyses even to the study of airway epithelial regeneration using airway organoids.3 Visualization is achieved by the genomic introduction of fluorophore-containing peptides via lentiviral transduction. Imaging and readout are described using a confocal microscope and AI-supported analysis of cell parameters by fusion protein Occludin-mEmerald-expressing cells.Note: This protocol describes a pipeline of experiments, which means that it extends over at least 6–7 weeks in its entirety and thus requires respective time management. The protocol is greatly shortened in the case of already running organoid cultures or prepared virus particles.
